a sealed letter from an old employer
a numbered note at the foot of a page
a word explained by the page it points to

intro.en: The Latin verb of carrying takes a prefix of return and a noun ending, and the noun comes to mean both a mention and the proof behind it.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「携带」动词接上表返回的前缀与名词词尾，名词便同时表示「提及」与「提及背后的凭据」。

latinIntro.en: The stem is ferre, to carry, with re- meaning back and -entia forming the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 ferre（携带），re- 表「往回」，-entia 构成名词。

definition_en: to remove impurities from a substance; to improve something by small careful changes; to make manners or taste more polished
core_image: 糖浆在铜锅里慢慢熬成雪白的结晶
scene: 糖厂的铜锅冒着热气，浓稠的糖浆被一遍遍撇去浮沫。The plant refines raw sugar before it reaches the shops.
sceneCN: 这里 refines 是 refine 的第三人称单数，取「提炼」（第 1 个义项：除去杂质使物质纯净）；句意为工厂先把粗糖提炼，再送进商店。画面里可留意：冒热气的铜锅、被撇去的浮沫。

senses.title: To purify a substance
senses.definition: to remove impurities from oil, sugar, or metal
senses.definitionCN: 除去油、糖或金属中的杂质
senses.example: The plant refines raw sugar before it reaches the shops.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先把粗糖提炼，再送进商店。
senses.why: Fine here means pure, and the prefix says the work is done again and again until the last impurity is gone.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 fine 意为纯净，前缀则表示这道工序要反复进行，直到最后一点杂质也被除去。

senses.title: To improve by small changes
senses.definition: to make a method, design, or skill better through careful adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 通过细致的调整使方法、设计或技能更好
senses.example: The team spent a month refining the test before the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在发布前花了一个月改进这项测试。
senses.why: Improving a method is a slow filtering of ideas: each round removes what does not work.
senses.whyCN: 改良方法是对想法进行缓慢的过滤：每一轮都去掉行不通的部分。

senses.title: To make polished
senses.definition: to make manners, taste, or language more delicate and cultivated
senses.definitionCN: 使举止、品味或语言更细腻有教养
senses.example: Years abroad had refined her taste in music.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的海外生活使她的音乐品味变得精细。
senses.why: The same word moves from metal to manners: what is refined has been worked over until the coarse part is gone.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从金属转到举止：凡被 refined 的东西，都是经过反复打磨，粗陋之处已去。

intro.en: Refine is to make fine: the Latin limit becomes a finish, and repeated finishing removes what is coarse.
intro.cn: refine 就是「使精细」：拉丁语的「界限」变成了「完工」，而反复的精加工去掉了粗糙之处。

items.en: Finis meant an end, a limit, or a boundary, and it grew into words about finishing and fineness.
items.cn: finis 意为终点、界限或边界，由此生长出关于「完成」与「精细」的词。

items.en: French affiner meant to make fine or pure, built on fin, the same root as finis.
items.cn: 法语 affiner 意为使精细或纯净，其词根 fin 与 finis 同源。

items.en: Middle French raffiner added the prefix of repetition to affiner and named the purifying of sugar and metal.
items.cn: 中期法语 raffiner 在 affiner 前加上表重复的前缀，用来指炼糖与炼金属。

items.en: English borrowed the word for purifying substances and soon extended it to improving anything.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词表示提纯物质，很快又扩展到改进任何事物。

items.en: The sense of polished manners grew in the eighteenth century, when taste itself was thought of as something to be refined.
items.cn: 「举止文雅」这一义在十八世纪发展起来，那时品味本身也被视为可以精炼的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin finis; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of purifying and improving.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 finis 构成的词；近义组收表示提纯与改进的动词。

entries.definition: To rub until smooth or to make more elegant.
To develop a taste or skill.

normalIntro.en: The word says make fine: take a coarse thing and work it until only the fine part is left.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「使精细」：拿一件粗糙的东西反复加工，直到只剩精细的部分。

normal.en: Re plus fine: to make something fine again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 fine：反复把某物做得更精细。

normal.en: A refinery is the place where crude oil is refined.
normal.cn: refinery 就是原油被提炼的地方。

normal.en: Refine a method means to take out the steps that do not work.
normal.cn: refine a method 指去掉行不通的步骤。

normal.en: Refined sugar is white; refined manners are smooth.
normal.cn: 精炼的糖是白的，文雅的举止是顺的。

normal.en: The noun is refinement, the adjective refined.
normal.cn: 名词是 refinement，形容词是 refined。

abstract.en: Refining is less about adding than about removing.
abstract.cn: 精炼与其说是添加，不如说是去除。

abstract.en: A person is refined by what they have learned to leave out.
abstract.cn: 一个人之所以文雅，在于学会了舍弃什么。

abstract.en: Every craft improves by small refinements no one notices.
abstract.cn: 每一门手艺都靠无人注意的细小改良而进步。

examples.en: The plant refines raw sugar before it reaches the shops.
examples.cn: 工厂先把粗糖提炼，再送进商店。

examples.en: The team spent a month refining the test before the launch.
examples.cn: 团队在发布前花了一个月改进这项测试。

examples.en: Years abroad had refined her taste in music.
examples.cn: 多年的海外生活使她的音乐品味变得精细。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（反复）加 fine（精细）：反复地弄精细，就是提炼杂质、改进方法、打磨举止。

root: 拉丁 finis（界限、终点）→ 法语 affiner（使精细）→ 中期法语 raffiner → 英语 refine；同族有 refinement、refinery，形近的 define、confine、finish 也出自 finis。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making fine; the senses move from removing impurities in matter, to improving a method by small steps, to polishing manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使精细」；义项从除去物质中的杂质，到以小步改进方法，再到打磨举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick syrup in a copper pan slowly turning into white crystals.
core.cn: 核心意象：铜锅里的浓糖浆慢慢熬成雪白的结晶。

branches.en: white sugar in a paper bag
a test rewritten five times
a quiet, well-chosen compliment
branches.cn: 一句克制而得体的赞美

branches.en: impurities taken out of a process
a sharpened skill and a softened manner
branches.cn: 更精的技术与更柔的举止

intro.en: A Latin word for a boundary turns into a verb of finishing, and the prefix of repetition turns finishing into refining.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「边界」的词转成表「完成」的动词，表重复的前缀又把「完成」变成「精炼」。

latinIntro.en: The base is finis, a limit or end, which also gives the Latin verb finire, to finish.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 finis（界限、终点），它也给出拉丁动词 finire（完成）。

definition_zh: 精炼；改良；精细化；优雅；提纯
definition_en: the act of making something more precise, polished or pure, or the quality of being polished
core_image: 一块粗铁矿在炉中反复熔炼，表面逐渐变得光洁
scene: 这里指「精炼」。 Repeated refinement of the model reduced its error from ten percent to two.
sceneCN: 这里 refinement 指「逐步精细化」（第 1 个义项：通过反复调整使结果更精确）；句意：对模型的反复精细化把误差从百分之十降到百分之二。图中可辨识物件：模型曲线、误差刻度、迭代箭头、砂纸。

pos.zh: 精炼；改良；精细化；优雅；提纯；（复数）细微改进

senses.title: Making more precise
senses.titleCN: 精细化：通过反复调整使更精确
senses.definition: the act of improving something by small repeated changes that make it more exact
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复的小改动使某物更精确的行为
senses.example: Repeated refinement of the model cut its error from ten percent to two.
senses.exampleCN: 对模型的反复精细化把误差从百分之十降到百分之二。
senses.why: The noun comes from refine, which joins re- 'again' to finire 'to make fine or end'; refinement is the process of making something finer step by step.
senses.whyCN: 该名词出自 refine，后者把 re-「再次」与 finire「使精细、结束」结合；refinement 就是一步步使事物更精细的过程。

senses.title: Elegance of manner
senses.titleCN: 举止优雅：教养与分寸感
senses.definition: the quality of polished, cultivated behaviour or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 经过打磨的、有教养的举止或外表的品质
senses.example: Her refinement showed in the way she listened without interrupting.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教养体现在她听人说话从不打断。
senses.why: The physical sense of removing coarse material became social: a person can be 'fined' by education until roughness is gone.
senses.whyCN: 去除粗料的物理义转向社会领域：人可以经教育「被精炼」，直到粗粝消失。

senses.title: Purification of a substance
senses.titleCN: 提纯：把原料中的杂质去除
senses.definition: the industrial process of removing impurities from sugar, oil, metal or another raw material
senses.definitionCN: 从糖、油、金属或其他原料中去除杂质的工业过程
senses.example: Sugar refinement removes molasses and leaves white crystals.
senses.exampleCN: 制糖提纯去除糖蜜，留下白色结晶。
senses.why: This sense is the most literal: the substance is made fine by taking away what is coarse or unwanted.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项最字面：通过去掉粗劣或不需要的成分，使物质变精细。

senses.title: Technical iteration
senses.titleCN: 技术迭代：网格或算法逐步加密
senses.definition: in computing and engineering, a repeated tightening of a mesh, model or estimate until it meets a tolerance
senses.definitionCN: 在计算与工程中，对网格、模型或估计反复加密，直到满足容差
senses.example: Mesh refinement near the wing tip improved the simulation.
senses.exampleCN: 翼尖附近的网格加密改善了模拟结果。
senses.why: Numerical work speaks of refinement when the grid is made finer; the word keeps its literal sense of reducing coarseness.
senses.whyCN: 数值工作把网格变细称为 refinement；该词保留了「减少粗糙度」的字面义。

senses.title: Improving a theory
senses.titleCN: 理论完善：补足漏洞与例外
senses.definition: the act of revising a theory or explanation to account for more cases and fewer errors
senses.definitionCN: 修订理论或解释，使其覆盖更多情形、减少错误的行为
senses.example: The refinement of the theory followed years of contrary evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这一理论的完善是在多年反证之后才实现的。
senses.why: A theory is treated like a raw material: each revision removes a defect, and the result is a finer version of the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 理论被当成原料：每次修订去掉一个缺陷，结果是同一事物的更精细版本。

senses.title: Social polish
senses.titleCN: 社交修养：礼节上的打磨
senses.definition: training in etiquette and courteous habits, often associated with a particular social class
senses.definitionCN: 在礼节与礼貌习惯上的训练，常与特定社会阶层相关
senses.example: The finishing school promised to teach refinement and poise.
senses.exampleCN: 这所精修学校承诺教授社交修养与仪态。
senses.why: Social class turned polish into a marker: refinement became something one could acquire and display.
senses.whyCN: 社会阶层把「打磨」变成标记：修养成了可以习得并展示的东西。

senses.title: Discriminating taste
senses.titleCN: 鉴赏力：能分辨细微差别
senses.definition: the ability to notice small differences in quality, especially in art, food or music
senses.definitionCN: 察觉质量细微差别的能力，尤指在艺术、饮食或音乐方面
senses.example: Her refinement of taste let her spot the counterfeit at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她的鉴赏力让她立刻看出赝品。
senses.why: A refined instrument detects fine distinctions; applied to taste, refinement names the same sensitivity.
senses.whyCN: 精密的仪器能察觉细微差别；用于品味时，refinement 命名的正是这种敏感度。

senses.title: Adding distinctions
senses.titleCN: 细化区分：在定义中补入更细的差别
senses.definition: in logic and writing, the addition of distinctions that make a statement more exact
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与写作中，补入使陈述更精确的区分
senses.example: The final refinement distinguished two senses that had been conflated.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的细化区分了此前被混为一谈的两个义项。
senses.why: Here finis 'boundary' surfaces: refinement draws finer boundaries, separating what had been one blurry category.
senses.whyCN: 这里 finis「边界」浮现出来：refinement 画出更细的边界，把原先模糊的一类分开。

intro.en: Refinement is the noun of refine, an English verb built from re- 'again' and the Latin-derived root finire 'to bound, make fine'. It is not borrowed whole from Latin.
intro.cn: refinement 是 refine 的名词，而 refine 是由 re-「再次」与拉丁来源词根 finire「划定边界、使精细」构成的英语动词，并非整体借自拉丁。

items.en: Latin finis meant 'end, boundary, limit'. It produced finire 'to bound, limit', and the adjective finus or finitus 'fine, finished'.
items.cn: 拉丁 finis 意为「终点、边界、限度」，由此产生 finire「划定界限、限制」以及形容词 finitus「精细的、完成的」。

items.en: Old French refiner meant 'to purify, make fine', especially for sugar and metal. The re- here intensifies or repeats the making-fine.
items.cn: 古法语 refiner 意为「提纯、使精细」，尤用于糖与金属；其中的 re- 加强或重复「使精细」的动作。

items.en: English refine appears in the sixteenth century with the sense 'to purify a substance', then extends to language, manners and ideas.
items.cn: 英语动词 refine 于 16 世纪出现，意为「提纯物质」，随后扩展到语言、举止与观念。

items.en: Refinement follows refine + -ment, the noun suffix from Latin -mentum, naming the act or its result.
items.cn: refinement 由 refine 加 -ment 构成，后者出自拉丁 -mentum，命名动作或其结果。

items.en: By the seventeenth century refinement also named cultivated manners, and later fastidious taste.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，refinement 也指有教养的举止，后来又指挑剔的品味。

items.en: The exact first English date is uncertain, and whether the social sense entered directly from French usage is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与语义传入路径）：英语首见确切年代存疑；社会义是否直接由法语用法传入，尚无定论。

note.en: The first group separates the refine family; the second gives near-synonyms for improvement, purity or elegance.
note.cn: 第一组区分 refine 词族；第二组给出关于改良、纯净或优雅的近义词。

entries.definition: To purify or make more exact. Refinement is the process or a single improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 指提纯或使更精确；refinement 是过程或一次改进。

entries.definition: Describing a purified substance or a cultivated person. It describes the result, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容提纯的物质或有教养的人；描述结果，而非动作。

entries.definition: A plant where oil or sugar is refined. It is a building, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 指炼油或制糖的工厂；是建筑，不是过程。

entries.definition: A person or machine that refines. It names the doer, while refinement names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行精炼的人或机器；命名施动者，而 refinement 命名动作。

entries.definition: Any change for the better. Refinement usually implies small, repeated, precision-oriented changes.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何变好的改变；refinement 通常暗示细小、反复、以精确为目标的改动。

entries.definition: The removal of contaminants. It overlaps sense 3 but says nothing about elegance or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指去除污染物；与第 3 个义项重叠，但不涉及优雅或精确。

entries.definition: A smooth surface, or a final tidy-up. It stresses the visible finish more than structural precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指光滑表面或最后的整理；更强调可见的完成度，而非结构精确。

entries.definition: Grace and stylish simplicity. It is close to sense 2 but focuses on beauty rather than training.
entries.definitionCN: 指形式上的优雅与简洁；接近第 2 个义项，但侧重美感而非训练。

entries.definition: A small, delicate difference or quality. It matches sense 7 but does not imply prior coarseness.
entries.definitionCN: 指细微而精巧的差别或品质；与第 7 个义项相合，但不暗示原先粗劣。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + finire 'make fine' + -ment: being made fine again and again.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ finire「使精细」+ -ment：被一次又一次做细。

normal.en: The family runs refine, refined, refiner, refinery, unrefined.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 refine、refined、refiner、refinery、unrefined。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: model refinement, sugar refinement, refinement of taste, further refinement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：模型细化、制糖提纯、品味修养、进一步细化。

normal.en: finis means boundary, so refinement draws finer lines between things.
normal.cn: finis 意为边界，因此 refinement 在事物之间画出更细的线。

normal.en: A refinery is the place; refinement is the process.
normal.cn: refinery 是场所，refinement 是过程。

abstract.en: Picture ore going through furnace after furnace until the surface turns bright.
abstract.cn: 想象矿石经过一座又一座炉子，直到表面变亮。

abstract.en: Picture a blurred line redrawn with a sharper pencil until two edges appear.
abstract.cn: 想象一条模糊的线被更尖的铅笔重画，直到显出两条边。

abstract.en: Picture a hand smoothing rough paper until the fingertips feel no grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把粗纸磨平，直到指尖摸不到纹理。

examples.en: The refinement of the telescope design took several prototypes.
examples.cn: 望远镜设计的改进用了几台原型机。

examples.en: Refinement of the raw sugar takes place at a mill near the coast.
examples.cn: 原糖的提纯在海岸附近的一家糖厂进行。

examples.en: Her refinement was evident in small courtesies, not in display.
examples.cn: 她的修养体现在细小的礼貌，而非炫耀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ fine（精细）」——一遍遍做到更细 → refinement 精炼、精细化

root: 拉丁 finis「边界、终点」→ finire「划定界限、使精细」→ 古法语 refiner「提纯」→ 英语 refine + -ment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses refine different materials: a model, a manner, a substance, a mesh, a theory, a social style, a taste, and a definition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项精炼的对象各不相同：模型、举止、物质、网格、理论、社交风格、品味与定义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ore passing through furnace after furnace until the surface shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：矿石经过一座座炉子，直到表面发亮。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND PROCESS: coarse matter or an imprecise result is made fine.
branches.cn: 材料与过程：粗料或不精确的结果被做细。

branches.en: SOCIAL SURFACE: roughness is removed from behaviour, and polish becomes a class marker.
branches.cn: 社交表面：举止的粗粝被去除，打磨成为阶层标记。

branches.en: NUMERICAL GRID: the mesh is made finer until the tolerance is met.
branches.cn: 数值网格：网格被加密，直到满足容差。

branches.en: THEORY: revisions remove defects from an explanation.
branches.cn: 理论：修订为解释去除缺陷。

branches.en: PERCEPTION AND DEFINITION: finer distinctions are heard, seen, or written into a statement.
branches.cn: 感知与定义：更细的差别被听见、看见，或被写进陈述。

intro.en: Refinement is an English noun of action: a Latin root for boundary and fineness, a French-influenced verb, and the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: refinement 是英语动作名词：一个表示边界与精细的拉丁词根，一个受法语影响的动词，以及名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The finis family includes finish, finite, infinite, define, final, finance and refine; all turn on the idea of a boundary or an end.
latinIntro.cn: finis 词族包括 finish、finite、infinite、define、final、finance、refine，核心都围绕边界或终点。

items.meaning: the act or result of making fine
items.meaningCN: 使变精细的动作或结果
items.example: The refinement of the lens improved resolution.
items.exampleCN: 镜头的改进提高了分辨率。

items.meaning: to purify or make more exact
items.example: The team refined the estimate with new data.
items.exampleCN: 团队用新数据细化了估算。

items.meaning: one who or that which refines
items.example: The refiner removed sulfur from the metal.
items.exampleCN: 精炼者从金属中去除了硫。
术语表为每个词下定义。

items.example: She finished the report at midnight.

latinEntries.meaning: to bound, limit; to make fine
suffix forming nouns of act or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成动作或结果名词的后缀

definition_en: to throw back light, heat, or sound; to show or express something; to think carefully about
core_image: 静止的湖面把整排山影倒映出来
scene: 清晨湖面没有一丝风，对岸的山被完整地映在水里。The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
sceneCN: 这里 reflected 是 reflect 的过去式，取「反射、映出」（第 1 个义项：把光或影像折回）；句意为静止的水面映出了整排山峦。画面里可留意：没有波纹的湖面、水中的山影。

senses.title: To throw back
senses.definition: to send back light, heat, or sound from a surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面把光、热或声音送回去
senses.example: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
senses.exampleCN: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。
senses.why: The Latin verb is to bend back: a ray meets a surface and is bent away from it, as if the surface refused to keep it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「弯回去」：光线碰到表面后被折开，仿佛表面不肯留下它。

senses.title: To show or stand for
senses.definition: to show the nature or state of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某事物的性质或状况
senses.example: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。
senses.why: A surface that shows an image is a natural picture of a society that shows its own condition in its records.
senses.whyCN: 能映出影像的表面，自然成了「社会借记录显现自身状况」这一用法的比喻。

senses.title: To think carefully
senses.definition: to turn the mind back on an idea or an experience
senses.definitionCN: 把心思转回到某个想法或经历上
senses.example: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。
senses.why: Thinking is a bending back of attention: the mind leaves the outer scene and returns to what it already holds.
senses.whyCN: 思考是注意力的折返：心思离开外在景象，回到自己已经拥有的东西上。

intro.en: Reflect is to bend back; the word begins with light and ends with thought, and the path between them is a single metaphor.
intro.cn: reflect 意为「弯回去」；这个词从光开始，到思想结束，而两者之间的路径只是一个比喻。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend or curve, the base of a family of words about turning.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲，是表示「转向」的词族的词根。

items.en: Reflectere joined re-, back, with flectere and meant to bend or turn back.
items.cn: reflectere 由 re-（往回）与 flectere 组成，意为弯回去或转回去。

items.en: Natural philosophers used the word first for rays of light bent back from a surface.
items.cn: 自然哲学家最先用这个词指从表面折回的光线。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the same word described an image in a mirror and a mind turned back on itself.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，同一个词既指镜中的影像，也指回转自身的头脑。

items.en: The sense of showing a condition grew from the mirror: a record reflects what produced it.
items.cn: 「显现状况」这一义从镜子发展而来：一份记录会映出产生它的那个东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin flectere; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of showing, mirroring, and thinking.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 flectere 构成的动词；近义组收表示映现与思考的动词。

entries.definition: To change the pitch or form of a word.

normalIntro.en: The word is a bending back, whether of light from water or of attention from the world to the self.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「弯回去」，既可以是水面对光的折返，也可以是注意力从外界折回自身。

normal.en: Re plus flectere, back plus bend: light bends back from the water.
normal.cn: re 加 flectere，往回加弯：光从水面弯回来。

normal.en: A mirror reflects your face; a report reflects the facts.
normal.cn: 镜子映出你的脸，报告映出事实。

normal.en: Reflect on a question means to bend your mind back to it.
normal.cn: reflect on a question 指把心思折回到这个问题上。

normal.en: Reflective people think; reflective surfaces shine.
normal.cn: reflective 的人爱思考，reflective 的表面会反光。

normal.en: Do not confuse reflect with deflect, which turns things aside.
normal.cn: 别把 reflect 与 deflect 弄混，后者是把东西拨到一边。

abstract.en: To reflect is to let what is outside pass through you and come back changed.
abstract.cn: 反射，就是让外界之物穿过你，再以改变过的样子回来。

abstract.en: A society is known by what it chooses to reflect on.
abstract.cn: 一个社会因它选择反思什么而为人所知。

abstract.en: The mirror and the mind use the same verb because both return an image.
abstract.cn: 镜子与头脑共用同一个动词，因为两者都送回一个影像。

examples.en: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
examples.cn: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。

examples.en: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。

examples.en: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 flect（弯）：光弯回来是反射，事实弯回来是反映，心思弯回来是思考。

root: 拉丁 flectere（弯曲）→ reflectere（弯回去）→ 英语 reflect；同族有 reflection、reflective、reflector，形近的 deflect、inflect、reflex 共用 flectere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bending back; the senses move from a ray returned by a surface, to a record showing its source, to a mind turned back on itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「弯回去」；义项从表面送回的光线，到映出其来源的记录，再到回转自身的头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a windless lake holding the whole line of hills.
core.cn: 核心意象：无风的湖面托着整排山影。

branches.en: hills upside down in water
a report that sounds like the village
a window seat and a long pause
branches.cn: 窗边的座位与长久的停顿

branches.en: an image that tells the truth of its source
a fact seen and then weighed
branches.cn: 看见事实之后加以权衡

intro.en: A Latin verb of bending takes a prefix of return, and the compound passes from rays of light to the movement of thought.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「弯曲」动词接上表返回的前缀，这个复合词便从光线走到了思想的运动。

latinIntro.en: The base is flectere, to bend, with re- meaning back; the participle reflexus feeds the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 flectere（弯曲），re- 表「往回」；分词 reflexus 供给名词形式。

definition_zh: 使恢复精神；刷新；使重新清晰
definition_en: to make someone feel less tired; to load a page or data again so that it is current; to make a memory clear again
core_image: 树荫下用凉水洗脸的人抬起头，长长呼出一口气
scene: 午后最热的时候，他在树荫下用凉水洗了把脸，抬起头长出一口气。A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
sceneCN: 这里 refreshed 是 refresh 的过去式，取「使恢复精神」（第 1 个义项：让人重新有精力）；句意为长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。画面里可留意：树荫、凉水、长出的那口气。

pos.zh: 使恢复精神；刷新；使重新清晰

derivatives.zh: 提神的；令人耳目一新的

senses.title: To restore energy
senses.definition: to make a tired person or body feel lively again
senses.definitionCN: 使疲倦的人或身体重新有精神
senses.example: A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。
senses.why: The prefix says again and the root says fresh: energy that had gone stale is brought back to its first state.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「再次」，词根意为「新鲜」：已经发蔫的精力被带回最初的状态。

senses.title: To load again
senses.definition: to load a page, a screen, or a set of data again so that it shows the latest state
senses.definitionCN: 重新载入网页、屏幕或数据，使其显示最新状态
senses.example: Refresh the page if the table still looks empty.
senses.exampleCN: 如果表格仍然空着，就刷新页面。
senses.why: A screen, like a tired body, holds an old picture; loading it again makes the picture current.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕和疲倦的身体一样，都存着旧的画面；重新载入便让画面变新。

senses.title: To make a memory clear
senses.definition: to bring a fact or a skill back into the mind clearly
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事实或技能清晰地唤回脑中
senses.example: Let me refresh your memory about the rules of the game.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你回忆一下比赛规则。
senses.why: A memory that has faded is made fresh again, so the word serves both the body and the mind.
senses.whyCN: 淡去的记忆被重新变新，所以这个词对身心都适用。

intro.en: Refresh is the Latin prefix re- laid on the Germanic word fresh; only the prefix is Latin, the root came to English from its own northern stock.
intro.cn: refresh 是拉丁前缀 re- 加在日耳曼语源的 fresh 上；只有前缀来自拉丁语，词根是从北方语族进入英语的。

items.en: A Germanic word for fresh, lively, or cool lies behind the English adjective.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中一个表示新鲜、有生气或清凉的词，是英语形容词的来源。

items.en: Old English fersc meant fresh, not salt, and it described water and food.
items.cn: 古英语 fersc 意为新鲜的、非腌制的，用来描述水与食物。

items.en: Old French freis reinforced the word with the sense of new and lively.
items.cn: 古法语 freis 以「新的、有生气的」之义强化了这个词。

items.en: Middle English fresh kept both the sense of new and the sense of not tired.
items.cn: 中古英语 fresh 同时保留「新」与「不疲倦」两义。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the Latin prefix re-, again, was added, and refresh meant to make fresh once more.
items.cn: 十六世纪加上拉丁前缀 re-（再次），refresh 便表示「使重新新鲜」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on fresh; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of renewing strength or data.
note.cn: 形近组收由 fresh 构成的词；近义组收表示恢复精力或更新数据的动词。

entries.definition: Food, drink, or rest that restores.
To bring back to life or strength.
To bring back to a former state.

normalIntro.en: The word is fresh plus again: a tired body, a stale page, or a faded memory is made fresh once more.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 fresh 加 again：疲倦的身体、过时的页面、淡去的记忆，都被重新变新。

normal.en: Re plus fresh: to make fresh again.
normal.cn: re 加 fresh：使重新变新鲜。

normal.en: A cool drink refreshes you on a hot day.
normal.cn: 大热天一杯冷饮让你精神一振。

normal.en: Press the button to refresh the page.
normal.cn: 按这个按钮刷新页面。

normal.en: Refresh your memory means to look the facts up again.
normal.cn: refresh your memory 指把事实再查一遍。

normal.en: The adjective refreshing describes what gives you this lift.
normal.cn: 形容词 refreshing 描述给你这种提振的东西。

abstract.en: Refreshment is not always rest; sometimes it is a change of work.
abstract.cn: 恢复精神未必靠休息，有时靠换一件工作。

abstract.en: A page reloads, but a mind needs more than a button.
abstract.cn: 页面可以重载，头脑却需要一个按钮之外的东西。

abstract.en: What refreshes a person is whatever returns them to their first energy.
abstract.cn: 能让人 refresh 的，是把他带回最初精力的东西。

examples.en: A cold shower refreshed him before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途开车前，一个冷水澡让他精神起来。

examples.en: Refresh the page if the table still looks empty.
examples.cn: 如果表格仍然空着，就刷新页面。

examples.en: Let me refresh your memory about the rules of the game.
examples.cn: 让我帮你回忆一下比赛规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再次）加 fresh（新鲜）：让身体再新鲜一次是提神，让页面再新鲜一次是刷新，让记忆再新鲜一次是想起来。

root: 拉丁前缀 re-（再次）＋ 日耳曼语源 fresh（新鲜，古英语 fersc）→ 英语 refresh；词根不是拉丁语，因此本词的拉丁条目只收前缀。同族有 refreshment、refreshing、refresher。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making fresh again; the senses move from a tired body, to a stale screen, to a faded memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使重新新鲜」；义项从疲倦的身体，到过时的屏幕，再到淡去的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man lifting his wet face in the shade, breathing out slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：树荫下用凉水洗脸后抬起头、缓缓呼气的人。

branches.en: a cold shower before a drive
a page loaded a second time
rules brought back to mind
a body and a memory both woken
branches.cn: 身体与记忆同时被唤醒

branches.en: data renewed as energy is renewed
branches.cn: 数据更新如同精力恢复

intro.en: A Latin prefix of repetition meets a Germanic adjective of freshness, and the compound means to make fresh once more.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表重复的前缀遇上日耳曼语表新鲜的形容词，合成词便表示「使重新新鲜」。

latinIntro.en: Only re- is Latin here; fresh descends from Old English fersc, so no Latin root entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里只有 re- 来自拉丁语；fresh 源自古英语 fersc，因此不列拉丁词根条目。

definition_en: a machine or cabinet that keeps food cold; a large cooling apparatus for storage
core_image: 厨房角落里嗡嗡作响的白色机器，门上贴满便签
scene: 厨房角落那台白色的机器整夜嗡嗡作响，门上贴着孩子的画和几张便签。She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 refrigerator 是「冰箱」（第 1 个义项：家用冷藏电器）；句意为她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。画面里可留意：白色机器、门上的画与便签、夜里的嗡鸣。

senses.title: A kitchen appliance
senses.definition: a household cabinet, usually electric, that keeps food cold
senses.definitionCN: 通常用电的、使食物保持低温的家用箱柜
senses.example: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。
senses.why: The Latin name is simply a thing that makes cold, and the kitchen cabinet is the most familiar such thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名称的意思就是「使冷的东西」，而厨房里的箱柜是最为人熟悉的那一个。

senses.title: A large cooling unit
senses.definition: a large machine or room used to keep goods cold in shops or industry
senses.definitionCN: 商店或工业中用来使货物保持低温的大型机器或房间
senses.example: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。
senses.why: The same word serves the home and the trade: both are boxes where cold is made and held.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词家用与商用都管：两者都是制造并保持低温的箱子。

intro.en: Refrigerator is a modern Latin name built from the verb to cool: it means the thing that makes cold.
intro.cn: refrigerator 是用「使冷」的动词构成的近代拉丁名称，意思就是「使冷的东西」。

items.en: Frigus meant cold, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: frigus 意为寒冷，是整个词族的来源。

items.en: Frigerare meant to cool something, built on frigus.
items.cn: frigerare 意为使某物变冷，由 frigus 构成。

items.en: Refrigerare added re- and meant to cool down or refresh, often of fevered patients.
items.cn: refrigerare 加上 re-，意为使冷却或使清爽，常用于发热的病人。

items.en: Writers of the nineteenth century formed refrigerator from the verb and the ending -ator, one that does.
items.cn: 十九世纪的写作者用该动词加词尾 -ator（做某事者）造出 refrigerator。

items.en: English applied the name to the ice box, and later to the electric cabinet in every kitchen.
items.cn: 英语先用它指冰柜，后来又指每间厨房里的电动箱柜。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same cooling family; the near-meaning group gathers names for cold storage.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「制冷」词族的词；近义组收表冷藏器具的名称。

entries.definition: A compartment or machine for freezing food.
A container that keeps things cool.
An old-fashioned box cooled with ice.

normalIntro.en: The word is literally a cold-maker: a box that produces and holds cold so that food lasts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「造冷者」：一个制造并保持低温、让食物放得更久的箱子。

normal.en: Frigus is cold, and the machine is the thing that makes cold.
normal.cn: frigus 是寒冷，而这台机器就是造冷的东西。

normal.en: Refrigerate the milk, and the refrigerator keeps it cold.
normal.cn: 把牛奶冷藏，冰箱就让它保持低温。

normal.en: The ending ator marks the doer, as in elevator and generator.
normal.cn: 词尾 ator 标记「做某事者」，如 elevator 与 generator。

normal.en: A walk-in refrigerator is big enough to walk inside.
normal.cn: walk-in refrigerator 大到可以走进去。

normal.en: Refrigeration is the process; the refrigerator is the box.
normal.cn: refrigeration 是过程，refrigerator 是箱子。

abstract.en: Cold is not created but moved, and the machine only moves it faster.
abstract.cn: 冷并非被造出，只是被搬运，而机器只是搬得更快。

abstract.en: A refrigerator is a promise that tomorrow will taste like today.
abstract.cn: 冰箱是一个承诺：明天的味道会像今天一样。

abstract.en: The same Latin verb once cooled a fever and now cools a bottle.
abstract.cn: 同一个拉丁动词曾给发热者降温，如今给瓶子降温。

examples.en: She kept the milk in the refrigerator overnight.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶放在冰箱里过夜。

examples.en: The fish was stored in a walk-in refrigerator behind the shop.
examples.cn: 鱼存放在店后的大型冷藏库里。

examples.en: Open the refrigerator door and let the cold air out slowly.
examples.cn: 打开冰箱门，让冷气慢慢散出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（加强）加 friger（冷）加 ator（做某事者）：专门造冷的东西，就是冰箱。

root: 拉丁 frigus（寒冷）→ frigerare（使冷）→ refrigerare（使冷却）→ 近代拉丁 refrigerator（造冷者）→ 英语 refrigerator；同族有 refrigerate、refrigeration、refrigerant。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cold-maker; the senses move from the household cabinet to the large cooling room of a shop.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造冷之物」；义项从家用箱柜，到商店里的大型冷藏库。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white machine humming all night in a kitchen corner, covered with notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房角落里嗡嗡作响、贴满便签的白色机器。

branches.en: milk on a kitchen shelf
a cold room behind a fish shop
the same cold in a home and a trade
branches.cn: 家中与店里的同一种冷

branches.en: a child's drawing taped to the door
a heavy door that seals a room

intro.en: A Latin word for cold becomes a verb of cooling, and the agent ending then names the machine that does it.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「寒冷」的词先变成「使冷」的动词，施动者词尾随后命名做这件事的机器。

latinIntro.en: The base is frigus, cold, with frigerare to cool, re- again, and -ator one who does.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 frigus（寒冷），frigerare 意为使冷，re- 表「再次」，-ator 指做某事者。

definition_en: money paid back to someone, or to pay money back to someone
core_image: 一叠钞票沿着来时的路，退回付款人手里
scene: 顾客发现外套袖口有破洞，回到店里出示小票，店员把货款原样退回他的卡里。When the customer brought back the torn coat, the shop gave him a full refund.
sceneCN: 这里 refund 是「退款」（第 1 个义项：退回给付款人的那笔钱）；句意：顾客把破了的外套拿回店里时，店家给了他全额退款。

derivatives.zh: refund 加后缀 -able，义为「可退还的」
否定前缀 non- 加 refundable，义为「不可退还的」
refund 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「退款」；在金融里也指债务的再融资

senses.title: Money paid back
senses.definition: money that is given back to a customer who has paid for goods or a service
senses.definitionCN: 退还给已付款顾客的那笔钱
senses.example: She kept the receipt in case she needed a refund.
senses.exampleCN: 她留着收据，以备需要退款。
senses.why: Refund begins as a pouring back: the Latin verb means to pour back, and the first English sense is the money that flows back to the payer.
senses.whyCN: refund 最初是「倒回去」：拉丁语动词意为把东西倒回原处，所以最早的英语义项就是流回付款人手里的那笔钱。

senses.title: To give money back
senses.definition: to return money to someone who has paid for something
senses.definitionCN: 把钱退还给为某物付过款的人
senses.example: The airline refunded the ticket price after the flight was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 航班取消后，航空公司退还了机票款。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical image of pouring the money back along the path it came by.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了把钱沿原路倒回这一具体意象。

senses.title: A tax refund
senses.definition: money that a tax office returns when someone has paid more tax than is owed
senses.definitionCN: 税务机关在纳税人多缴税款后退回的钱
senses.example: He used his tax refund to pay off the credit card.
senses.exampleCN: 他用退税款还清了信用卡。
senses.why: Modern tax systems reuse the pouring-back image for money the state returns.
senses.whyCN: 现代税制沿用了倒回这一意象，用来指国家退回的钱。

senses.title: A deposit returned
senses.definition: money given back when a deposit is released or a service has not been used
senses.definitionCN: 押金退还或服务未使用时退回的钱
senses.example: The landlord agreed to a refund of the cleaning deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 房东同意退还清洁押金。
senses.why: Any sum held in advance can flow back, so deposits and unused fees join the refund family.
senses.whyCN: 任何预先收下的款项都可能倒流回来，于是押金与未使用的费用也进入了 refund 的义场。

senses.title: To reimburse an expense
senses.definition: to pay back money that someone has already spent on behalf of another party
senses.definitionCN: 把某人替他人垫付的钱还给他
senses.example: The company will refund your travel costs within ten days.
senses.exampleCN: 公司会在十天内退还你的差旅费用。
senses.why: Business expense claims extend the verb from a purchase to any cost paid out for another party.
senses.whyCN: 商务报销把动词从一笔购物扩展到任何替他人垫付的费用。

intro.en: Refund comes from Latin refundere, to pour back or give back, from re-, back, and fundere, to pour; the noun refund, the sum returned, grew out of the verb in English.
intro.cn: refund 来自拉丁语 refundere（倒回、归还），由 re-（回）加 fundere（倒、倾注）构成；表示退款的名词义则是在英语里从动词长出来的。

items.en: Fundere means to pour, and English fusion comes from the same verb.
items.cn: fundere 意为倒、倾注，英语 fusion 也出自同一个动词。

items.en: Re- means back, so refundere is to pour back, hence to give back what was received.
items.cn: re- 表示回，所以 refundere 就是倒回去，引申为把收下的东西归还。

items.en: Old French refunder carries the giving-back verb into French.
items.cn: 古法语 refunder 把这个表示归还的动词带进法语。

items.en: English refund first appears as a verb meaning to give back money or restore something taken.
items.cn: 英语 refund 最初是动词，意为退还钱款或归还原物。

items.en: The noun refund settles into shop, ticket, and tax use, naming the sum that comes back.
items.cn: 名词 refund 在商店、票务与税务场景里固定下来，专指退回的那笔钱。

note.en: Refund belongs to the Latin pouring family of fundere and refundere, with refundable and refunding beside it, and it sits near rebate, reimbursement, and repayment.
note.cn: refund 属于拉丁语「倒、倾注」词族，旁边有 refundable 与 refunding，并与 rebate、reimbursement、repayment 意义相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 可退还的，由 refund 加 -able 构成

entries.definition: the act of paying money back
entries.definitionCN: 退款行为，也可指债务再融资

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 基金；资金，只是拼写相近，词源不同：fund 出自拉丁语 fundus（底部、地产）

entries.definition: a partial return of money paid, often as a discount
entries.definitionCN: 回扣；部分退款，通常是价格优惠的一部分

entries.definition: money paid back for costs someone has already met
entries.definitionCN: 报销款，指补偿他人已垫付的费用

entries.definition: money paid back against a loan or a debt
entries.definitionCN: 还款，多指偿还借款或债务

normalIntro.en: Refund joins re-, back, to the Latin verb fundere, to pour, so the word pictures money poured back to its owner.
normalIntro.cn: refund 由 re-（回）加拉丁语动词 fundere（倒、倾注）构成，画面就是把钱倒回主人手里。

normal.en: Re- means back and fundere means to pour: refund is to pour back.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，fundere 表示倒，refund 就是把东西倒回去。

normal.en: The verb refund is stressed on the second syllable, the noun on the first.
normal.cn: 动词 refund 重音在后，名词 refund 重音在前。

normal.en: A full refund returns every penny the customer paid.
normal.cn: full refund 是把顾客付的每一分钱都退回去。

normal.en: A tax refund comes from the tax office, not from a shop.
normal.cn: tax refund 来自税务部门，而不是商店。

normal.en: Refundable means the money can be returned; non-refundable means it cannot.
normal.cn: refundable 表示钱可以退，non-refundable 表示不能退。

abstract.en: Picture a shop assistant counting notes back into the hand of the customer.
abstract.cn: 想象店员把钞票数回顾客手里。

abstract.en: Picture money sliding back along the same path it came by.
abstract.cn: 想象钱沿着来时的路滑回去。

abstract.en: Picture a tax form with a small sum circled for return.
abstract.cn: 想象一张税表，上面圈出一小笔要退回的钱。

examples.en: The shop offered a refund without asking for a reason.
examples.cn: 商店没问原因就给了退款。

examples.en: He refunded the deposit two days after the inspection.
examples.cn: 他在检查后两天退还了押金。

examples.en: Only part of the fee was refunded to the students.
examples.cn: 只把一部分费用退还给了学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞返」——钱从柜台那头返回到你手上，就是退款；谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回、向后）+ fundere（倒、倾注）→ 拉丁语 refundere（倒回；归还）→ 古法语 refunder → 英语 refund，核心义「把钱倒回付款人手里」。另有同形词由 re- 加 fund（资金）构成，义为「重新融资」，与本词无关。

sensesIntro.en: Refund keeps the Latin image of pouring money back: it names the sum returned, the act of returning it, and the tax, deposit, and expense sums that flow back.
sensesIntro.cn: refund 保留拉丁语把钱倒回去的意象：既指退回的那笔钱，也指退钱这个动作，还延伸到退税款、押金退款与报销款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of notes handed back to the person who paid.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠钞票被交回给当初付款的人。

branches.en: The sum that comes back is the everyday noun sense.
branches.cn: 退回来的那笔钱是最日常的名词义项。

branches.en: The act of handing the money back is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 把钱交回去这个动作是动词义项。

branches.en: Tax offices return overpaid tax with the same image.
branches.cn: 税务机关用同一意象退回多缴的税。

branches.en: Deposits and unused fees flow back as well.
branches.cn: 押金与未使用的费用同样会倒流回来。

branches.en: Reimbursing a cost extends the verb to money spent for another party.
branches.cn: 报销把动词扩展到替他人垫付的费用。

intro.en: Refund is built on the Latin verb fundere, to pour, with the prefix re-, back: refundere means to pour back, and English later makes the noun refund from it.
intro.cn: refund 建在拉丁语动词 fundere（倒、倾注）之上，加上前缀 re-（回），refundere 即倒回去；英语后来又由它造出名词 refund。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back and fundere means to pour, so refundere means to pour back and, in use, to give back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 意为回，fundere 意为倒，所以 refundere 意为倒回去，实际使用时就是归还。

items.example: The prefix re- turns pouring into pouring back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把倒变成了倒回去。
refundere 由 re- 与 fundere 合成。

items.example: Old French refunder passes the verb to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 refunder 把这个动词传给英语。

items.example: English refund keeps the act of giving back.
items.exampleCN: 英语 refund 保留了归还这一动作。

items.example: The noun refund names the sum returned.
items.exampleCN: 名词 refund 指退回的那笔钱。

items.example: Refundable describes a fare that can be returned.
items.exampleCN: refundable 描述可以退的票款。
前缀 non- 构成 non-refundable。

items.example: Refunding appears in finance as well as in shops.
items.exampleCN: refunding 既见于商店，也见于金融。

definition_en: the act of saying no to an offer or a request; the act of not granting something
core_image: 合同被推回桌对面，一只手轻轻摇了摇头
scene: 招聘方把合同推回桌对面，摇了摇头，没有多说什么。Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 refusal 是「拒绝」（第 1 个义项：表示不接受、不答应）；句意为她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。画面里可留意：被推回的合同、轻轻摇头的手。

senses.title: The act of saying no
senses.definition: the act of declining an offer, an invitation, or an order
senses.definitionCN: 不接受提议、邀请或命令的行为
senses.example: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。
senses.why: The noun names the no itself, and the Latin verb behind it images a pouring back: the offer is returned to the one who made it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是「不」本身，而其背后的拉丁动词描绘「倒回去」：提议被退回给提出的人。

senses.title: The act of not granting
senses.definition: the act of withholding something that was asked for
senses.definitionCN: 不给予别人所求之物的行为
senses.example: The refusal of a visa left the whole family in limbo.
senses.exampleCN: 签证被拒，让整个家庭悬而未决。
senses.why: When what is turned back is a gift or a permission rather than an offer, the same noun means a withholding.
senses.whyCN: 当被退回的是赠予或许可而不是提议时，同一个名词就表示「不给」。

intro.en: Refusal is the noun of refuse, and its oldest image is a pouring back: what was offered is sent back to its source.
intro.cn: refusal 是 refuse 的名词，其最古老的意象是「倒回去」：被提供的东西被送回原处。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour, and its participle supplied the image of something poured out.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，其分词提供了「被倒出之物」的意象。

items.en: Refusare probably joined re-, back, with the participle of fundere, giving the sense of pouring back and so rejecting.
items.cn: refusare 很可能由 re-（往回）与 fundere 的分词构成，意为倒回去，因而表示拒绝。

items.en: Old French refuser meant to refuse or reject, and English took the verb from it.
items.cn: 古法语 refuser 意为拒绝或驳回，英语由此借入动词。

items.en: English added the noun ending -al and made refusal, the act of the verb.
items.cn: 英语加上名词词尾 -al 造出 refusal，表示该动词的行为。

items.en: In modern use a refusal can be polite or blunt, and the word often carries the weight of a broken expectation.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，拒绝可以是客气的，也可以是生硬的，这个词常带着期待落空的分量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin like refuse; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for saying no.
note.cn: 形近组收与 refuse 开头相近的词；近义组收表示「说不」的名词。

entries.definition: A statement that something is not true or not granted.
The act of refusing to accept.

normalIntro.en: The noun is a no made into a thing: an offer comes to the table and is pushed back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是把「不」变成一件东西：提议来到桌前，又被推了回去。

normal.en: Refuse is the act, refusal is the no itself.
normal.cn: refuse 是动作，refusal 是那个「不」本身。

normal.en: A blunt refusal leaves no room for argument.
normal.cn: a blunt refusal 不留争辩的余地。

normal.en: Refusal to comply with the order brought a fine.
normal.cn: 拒绝服从命令招来了罚款。

normal.en: The refusal of a visa is a no written on paper.
normal.cn: 签证被拒，是写在纸上的一声「不」。

normal.en: Refusal ends in al, the ending that turns verbs into acts.
normal.cn: refusal 以 al 结尾，这个词尾把动词变成行为。

abstract.en: A refusal can protect a person as often as it disappoints one.
abstract.cn: 拒绝既能保护一个人，也常让人失望。

abstract.en: The right to refuse is the smallest unit of freedom.
abstract.cn: 拒绝的权利，是自由最小的单位。

abstract.en: A clear refusal is kinder than a slow maybe.
abstract.cn: 明确的拒绝，比拖延的「也许」更善意。

examples.en: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 她拒签合同，让所有人都很意外。

examples.en: The refusal of a visa left the whole family in limbo.
examples.cn: 签证被拒，让整个家庭悬而未决。

examples.en: He met every question with a polite refusal to answer.
examples.cn: 他对每个问题都以礼貌的拒绝作答。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 fus（倒）加 al（名词尾）：把递过来的东西倒推回去，就是拒绝；把它变成一件事，就是 refusal。

root: 拉丁 fundere（倾倒）→ refusare（倒回、拒绝）→ 古法语 refuser → 英语 refuse；加 -al 构成 refusal。同族有 refuse、refusable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a returned offer; the senses move from declining what is offered to withholding what is asked.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被退回的提议」；义项从拒绝所提供之物，到不给予所请求之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a contract pushed back across a table with a shake of the head.
core.cn: 核心意象：合同被推回桌对面，一只手轻轻摇了摇头。

branches.en: a signed page left unsigned
branches.cn: 一页没有被签下的合同

branches.en: a visa stamped no
an offer returned and a request denied
branches.cn: 提议被退回，请求被驳回

branches.en: a polite sentence with no room to argue
branches.cn: 一句客气却无可争辩的话

branches.en: a door that stays shut

intro.en: A Latin verb of pouring takes a prefix of return, and a noun ending turns the act of pushing an offer back into a thing with a name.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「倾倒」动词接上表返回的前缀，名词词尾再把「把提议推回去」这个动作变成有名字的事物。

latinIntro.en: The base is fundere, to pour; re- means back, and -al forms the noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 fundere（倾倒）；re- 表「往回」，-al 构成表行为的名词。

definition_en: to consider someone or something in a particular way; respect or esteem; to look at steadily
core_image: 老师把一份作业翻看两遍，然后缓缓点头
scene: 老师把那份作业翻来覆去看了两遍，最后缓缓点了点头。The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 regarded 是 regard 的过去式，取「看待」（第 1 个义项：以某种眼光认为）；句意为老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。画面里可留意：翻看两遍的动作、缓缓点头。

senses.title: To consider in a way
senses.definition: to think of someone or something in a particular manner
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式认为某人或某物
senses.example: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。
senses.why: The word begins with a steady look: to regard a thing is first to fix the eyes on it, and then to fix a judgment on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始于凝神一看：先让目光落在某物上，再让判断落在它上面。

senses.title: Respect or esteem
senses.definition: a feeling of admiration and careful attention toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的钦佩与郑重对待
senses.example: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。
senses.why: When the steady look carries weight, it becomes esteem: the one who is looked at long is the one who is valued.
senses.whyCN: 当这种凝神注视带上分量，它就变成敬重：被看得最久的人，也是被看重的人。

senses.title: To look at steadily
senses.definition: to look at someone or something with attention, often without speaking
senses.definitionCN: 带着注意看某人或某物，常常不出声
senses.example: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense, and it keeps the original image of eyes held on a face.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的一义，它保留了「目光停在一个人脸上」的原始意象。

intro.en: Regard is a French word of watching: a Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix, and English received it as a steady look.
intro.cn: regard 是一个来自法语的「看」的词：日耳曼语的「看守」动词接上法语前缀，英语接收它时意为凝神注视。

items.en: A Germanic verb of watching and guarding lies behind the French word for looking.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表「看守、注视」的动词，是法语「看」这个词的后盾。

items.en: Old French garder meant to guard or keep, and English kept it as guard.
items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为看守、保留，英语把它保留为 guard。

items.en: Regarder added the intensive prefix re- and meant to look at closely.
items.cn: regarder 加上加强语气的前缀 re-，意为仔细地看。

items.en: English took regard as both a look and a care, and the verb followed the noun.
items.cn: 英语把 regard 同时用作「注视」与「关切」，动词义随后跟上。

items.en: High regard and kind regards grew from the same root: attention paid becomes respect, and respect becomes a greeting.
items.cn: high regard 与 kind regards 出自同一词根：投去的注意变成敬重，敬重又变成问候。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the French verb of guarding; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of judging and looking.
note.cn: 形近组收由法语「看守」动词构成的词；近义组收表示评判与观看的动词。

entries.definition: To think of in a certain way.
To regard in a particular way.

normalIntro.en: The word is a long look: first the eyes rest on a thing, then the mind decides what it is worth.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次长久的注视：先让目光停在某物上，再让心思判定它值多少。

normal.en: Regard as means to hold an opinion about something.
normal.cn: regard as 指对某物持某种看法。

normal.en: To regard a person is to look, and to regard them highly is to look up.
normal.cn: regard 一个人是看，regard 得高就是敬重。

normal.en: In this regard is a formal way of saying in this matter.
normal.cn: in this regard 是「在这方面」的正式说法。

normal.en: Give my regards means pass on my greetings.
normal.cn: give my regards 指代我问候。

normal.en: Regardless drops the regard, and carries on without looking.
normal.cn: regardless 丢掉了「看」，不瞧一眼就继续。

abstract.en: How we regard a person decides how we treat them.
abstract.cn: 我们如何看待一个人，决定了我们如何对待他。

abstract.en: To be held in high regard is to be looked at with care.
abstract.cn: 被十分敬重，就是被郑重地看待。

abstract.en: A regard that never becomes action is only a look.
abstract.cn: 从不化为行动的尊重，只是一眼注视。

examples.en: The teacher regarded the essay as the best in the class.
examples.cn: 老师认为这篇作文是全班最好的。

examples.en: The old craftsman is held in high regard by everyone in the town.
examples.cn: 镇上人人都十分敬重这位老匠人。

examples.en: She regarded the stranger for a long moment before answering.
examples.cn: 她注视了那陌生人好一会儿才答话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（一再）加 gard（看守、看）：一再地看一个人，就是在打量他、评价他、敬重他。

root: 日耳曼语 wardon（看守）→ 古法语 garder（看守）→ regarder（仔细看）→ 英语 regard；re- 在此是加强语气的前缀，词根并非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只列前缀以外的法语与英语形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a steady look; the senses move from forming a view, to holding someone in esteem, to watching silently.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「凝神的注视」；义项从形成看法，到把人放在敬重的位置，再到默默观看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher reading an essay twice and then nodding slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把一份作业翻看两遍，缓缓点头。

branches.en: an essay called the best
branches.cn: 被评为最好的一篇作文

branches.en: an old craftsman respected by a town
a stranger watched before an answer
branches.cn: 答话前被注视的陌生人

branches.en: a look that turns into a standing
watching first, judging after

intro.en: A Germanic verb of guarding took a French prefix of intensity, and the compound passed into English as a steady, weighing look.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语表「看守」的动词接上法语中表加强的前缀，这个复合词进入英语，意为凝神而带分量的注视。

latinIntro.en: The stem is the French garder of Germanic origin; re- here intensifies rather than repeats, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是源自日耳曼语的法语 garder；这里的 re- 表加强而非重复，因此不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: without being affected by something; paying no attention to a difficulty or a warning
core_image: 雨幕中的跑道上，一个人仍按原来的节奏跑圈
scene: 雨越下越大，操场上的人却没有停，仍按原来的节奏跑圈。The team kept training regardless of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 regardless 是「不管」（第 1 个义项：不受某事影响）；句意为球队不顾下雨，照常训练。画面里可留意：越来越大的雨、没有停下的脚步。

senses.title: Without being affected
senses.definition: in spite of something, without letting it change what happens
senses.definitionCN: 尽管有某事，也不让它改变要做的事
senses.example: The team kept training regardless of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 球队不顾下雨，照常训练。
senses.why: The suffix means without, and the stem means looking: the word describes a person who does not look at the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「没有」，词干意为「看」：这个词描述一个不去看障碍的人。

senses.title: In any case
senses.definition: used alone to mean that something will happen whatever else is true
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用时，表示无论其他情况如何某事都会发生
senses.example: The bridge may be closed, but we are going regardless.
senses.exampleCN: 桥也许封了，但无论如何我们都要去。
senses.why: The same ignoring of conditions becomes an adverb of stubborn intent: the plan goes on, rain or no rain.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对条件的无视，转为副词便表示倔强的意图：计划照走，下不下雨都一样。

intro.en: Regardless is regard with a suffix meaning without: it names the attitude of one who does not look at what stands in the way.
intro.cn: regardless 是 regard 加上意为「没有」的后缀：它命名一种不去看阻碍的态度。

items.en: The French verb meant to look at closely, and English shortened it to regard.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为仔细地看，英语把它简省为 regard。

items.en: Regard kept the sense of a look and of a care, both of which the suffix can cancel.
items.cn: regard 保留「看」与「关切」两义，而后缀能把两者都取消。

items.en: The English suffix -less comes from a Germanic word meaning free of or without.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -less 出自一个意为「没有、免于」的日耳曼词。

items.en: The adjective and adverb regardless appeared in the eighteenth century and spread quickly in speech.
items.cn: 形容词与副词 regardless 出现在十八世纪，并很快在口语中流行。

items.en: The phrase regardless of became the standard way to name a condition that is not allowed to matter.
items.cn: regardless of 这一短语成为表示「不把某条件当作回事」的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of looking and not looking; the near-meaning group gathers expressions of ignoring conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收表示「看」与「不看」的词；近义组收表示无视条件的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word says look-less: no looking at the obstacle, so the plan continues as it was.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词说的是「不看」：不看障碍，所以计划照旧继续。

normal.en: Regard plus less: without looking at the thing in the way.
normal.cn: regard 加 less：不去看挡路的东西。

normal.en: Regardless of the weather means the rain will not stop us.
normal.cn: regardless of the weather 指下雨也拦不住我们。

normal.en: Going regardless is a stubborn kind of courage.
normal.cn: going regardless 是一种倔强的勇气。

normal.en: The suffix less cancels the looking in regard.
normal.cn: 后缀 less 取消了 regard 中的「看」。

normal.en: Do not confuse regardless with regardful, which means full of care.
normal.cn: 别把 regardless 与 regardful 弄混，后者意为充满关切。

abstract.en: To act regardless is to decide that a warning will not be a reason.
abstract.cn: 不顾一切地行动，就是认定某个警告不能成为理由。

abstract.en: Some obstacles deserve a look before they are ignored.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍在被无视之前，值得先看一眼。

abstract.en: Courage without regard is often only haste.
abstract.cn: 不顾一切的勇气，常常只是急躁。

examples.en: The team kept training regardless of the rain.
examples.cn: 球队不顾下雨，照常训练。

examples.en: The bridge may be closed, but we are going regardless.
examples.cn: 桥也许封了，但无论如何我们都要去。

examples.en: She applied for the job regardless of her lack of experience.
examples.cn: 尽管缺乏经验，她还是申请了这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: regard（看）加 less（没有）：不去看条件与阻碍，就是「不管」「无论如何」。

root: 古法语 regarder（仔细看）→ 英语 regard（看待）＋ -less（没有）→ regardless；词根非拉丁语，因此不列拉丁条目。同族有 regard、disregard、regardful。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not looking at an obstacle; the senses move from an act done in spite of something to the adverb of going on anyway.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「不去看障碍」；义项从不顾某事而行动，到「无论如何也要去」的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner holding the same pace while the rain grows heavier.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨幕中的跑道上，一个人仍按原来的节奏跑圈。

branches.en: training in heavy rain
a trip made though the bridge is shut
branches.cn: 桥封了仍要出发的旅行

branches.en: a condition noted and then set aside
branches.cn: 注意到条件之后又把它放到一边

branches.en: a warning that changes nothing
the same pace kept to the end
branches.cn: 一直保持到终点的节奏

intro.en: A word of looking takes a suffix of without, and the compound names the choice not to look at what blocks the way.
intro.cn: 一个表「看」的词接上表「没有」的后缀，合成词便命名「选择不看挡路之物」的态度。

latinIntro.en: The stem regard is French of Germanic origin, and the suffix -less is English; no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 regard 是源自日耳曼语的法语词，后缀 -less 属英语，因此不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: to grow again after being lost or damaged, or to restore something to a working state
core_image: 断枝的切口处冒出一圈浅绿色的新芽，把旧疤顶开
scene: 把剪下来的柳条插进湿土里，切口很快冒出新芽。Cut willow stems regenerate quickly when they are laid in damp soil.
sceneCN: 这里 regenerate 指「重新长出新组织」（第 1 个义项：失去或受损的部位重新长出）；句意：剪下的柳条放进湿土后很快再生出新芽。图中可辨识物件：柳条切口、新芽、湿土、水痕。

pos.zh: 再生；使恢复；重建；更新（及物或不及物）

senses.title: Regrow a lost body part
senses.titleCN: 再生身体部分：长回失去的组织
senses.definition: to grow back a part of the body that has been lost or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 重新长出已失去或受损的身体部分
senses.example: Some lizards can regenerate a lost tail.
senses.exampleCN: 有些蜥蜴能再生失去的尾巴。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus generare 'to beget' means the body gives itself a second copy of the lost part.
senses.whyCN: re-「再一次」加 generare「生育」，意思是身体为自己再造一份失去的部分。

senses.title: Grow a new plant or stand
senses.titleCN: 植物更新：从残体长成新株
senses.definition: to produce new shoots or a new generation of plants from surviving roots or seed
senses.definitionCN: 从存活的根或种子长出新的枝条或新一代植株
senses.example: The coppiced hazel regenerates from its stump.
senses.exampleCN: 矮林作业后的榛树从树桩再生。
senses.why: plants keep growing points, so cutting back is not death but the start of another generation.
senses.whyCN: 植物保留着生长点，因此被截断不是死亡，而是另一代的开始。

senses.title: Revive a declining district
senses.titleCN: 复兴街区：让旧区重新有活力
senses.definition: to improve a declining urban area through investment and new activity
senses.definitionCN: 通过投资与新活动使衰退城区重新活跃
senses.example: The city regenerated the old harbour into a market district.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市把旧港区改造成集市街区。
senses.why: the biological image is applied to a district that grows new functions on an old frame.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象被用到城区：旧框架上长出新的功能。

senses.title: Restore the vigour of a system
senses.titleCN: 系统恢复活力：使重新运转
senses.definition: to restore the activity or health of an economy, institution or system
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、机构或系统恢复活动与健康
senses.example: Cheap power helped regenerate the region's industry.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价电力帮助该地区工业重新焕发活力。
senses.why: a system that was running down is made to run again, which is the same return as in the body.
senses.whyCN: 原本走向停摆的系统重新运转，这与身体上的回归是同一回事。

senses.title: Rebuild a degraded ecosystem
senses.definition: to restore the structure and function of a damaged ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 恢复受损生态系统的结构与功能
senses.example: Wetland plants regenerate the peat that fire destroyed.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地植物重建被火烧毁的泥炭。
senses.why: the verb takes an ecosystem as its object, so renewal is measured in structure and function rather than in cells.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以带生态系统作宾语，因此更新以结构与功能而非细胞来衡量。

senses.title: Renew a spent material
senses.titleCN: 材料再生：使旧材料可再用
senses.definition: to restore a used material or medium so that it can serve again
senses.definitionCN: 使使用过的材料或介质恢复可用
senses.example: The plant regenerates its ion-exchange resin with acid.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用酸使离子交换树脂再生。
senses.why: industry gives a material a second working life, borrowing the biological verb for a technical cycle.
senses.whyCN: 工业让材料获得第二个使用周期，把生物学动词借到技术循环上。

senses.title: Renew spiritually or morally
senses.titleCN: 精神重生：道德与心志的更新
senses.definition: to renew a person's spirit or moral life
senses.definitionCN: 更新一个人的精神或道德生活
senses.example: The retreat was meant to regenerate the volunteers' sense of purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这次静修意在更新志愿者的使命感。
senses.why: the oldest sense in English, where what grows again is not tissue but purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最早的义项，重新长出的不是组织，而是目标感。

senses.title: Recreate something from records
senses.titleCN: 由记录重建：让旧状态重现
senses.definition: to rebuild a lost object or state from stored information
senses.definitionCN: 依据保存的信息重建失去的物体或状态
senses.example: The team regenerated the damaged map from survey notes.
senses.exampleCN: 团队依据测量笔记重建了损坏的地图。
senses.why: when information survives, the object can be produced again; this is regeneration without living tissue.
senses.whyCN: 当信息还在，物体就能再被造出来；这是没有活组织的再生。

intro.en: Regenerate comes from Latin regenerare 'to bring forth again', built on re- and generare 'to beget' from genus 'birth, race'. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: regenerate 出自拉丁 regenerare「再次产生」，由 re- 与 generare「生育」构成，后者源自 genus「出生、族类」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Genus named birth, origin or kind; the stem gener- carries the idea of a line being brought into being.
items.cn: genus 指出生、来源或族类；词干 gener- 承载「使一条血脉产生」的意思。

items.en: Generare meant 'to beget, produce' and is the base of generate, generation and generous.
items.cn: generare 意为「生育、产生」，是 generate、generation 与 generous 的共同基础。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus generare gave regenerare 'to bring forth again', used of plants, bodies and the soul.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 generare 得 regenerare「再次产生」，用于植物、身体与灵魂。

items.en: The English verb is recorded in the sixteenth century, first in theological writing and then in medicine.
items.cn: 英语动词于 16 世纪有记录，先见于神学写作，后进入医学。

items.en: Eighteenth-century experiments on hydra and planarians gave the verb its modern laboratory sense.
items.cn: 18 世纪对水螅与涡虫的实验，赋予这个动词现代实验室含义。

items.en: The first date and the exact route from theology to biology are not fully recorded; dates here are approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代以及从神学到生物学的确切路径并无完整记录；此处年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same generare family; group two holds near meanings that differ in agency and scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 generare 词族的形近词；第二组是近义词，区别在于施动者与范围。

entries.tag: the noun of the same act
entries.definition: The process or instance of regrowing. It names the event, while regenerate names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指再生这一过程或实例；regeneration 命名事件，regenerate 命名动作。

entries.definition: To bring something into being for the first time. It lacks the idea of a second life.
entries.definitionCN: 指首次产生某物；不含「第二次生命」的意思。

entries.definition: To fall from a better to a worse state, built with de- 'down'. It is the opposite of regenerate.
entries.definitionCN: 指由较好状态退向较差状态，由 de-「向下」构成，与 regenerate 相反。

entries.definition: Describing something able to renew itself, such as regenerative agriculture. It does not name the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能够自我更新的事物，如再生农业；它不命名动作本身。

entries.definition: To grow again after being cut. It is the everyday word for plants and hair, with no wider institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指被剪后重新生长，是植物与头发的日常用词，没有更广的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a chosen earlier condition. It implies an agent doing the work, not self-renewal.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过有意的工作把某物带回选定的旧状态；暗含施动者，而非自行更新。

entries.definition: To make conscious or active again, from Latin vivere 'to live'. It suits practices and feelings more than tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指出自拉丁 vivere「活」的使复苏，多用于习俗与感受，少用于组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + generare 'to beget': to give birth to again.
normal.cn: re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」：再生一次。

normal.en: The family runs generate, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 generate、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: regenerate tissue, regenerate forests, regenerate a neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：再生组织、使森林更新、复兴街区。

normal.en: Biology pairs it with tissue; forestry pairs it with stump and seed tree.
normal.cn: 生物学把它与组织配对；林学把它与树桩、母树配对。

normal.en: Engineering pairs it with resin and catalyst: a material given a second working life.
normal.cn: 工程学把它与树脂、催化剂配对：材料获得第二个使用周期。

abstract.en: Picture a willow rod pushed into wet soil and sprouting at its cut end.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柳条插进湿土，在切口处抽芽。

abstract.en: Picture a rusted dock rebuilt into a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象生锈的码头被改建成集市广场。

abstract.en: Picture a burnt forest floor already dotted with green shoots.
abstract.cn: 想象烧过的林地地面已点缀着绿芽。

examples.en: The liver can regenerate much of its tissue after surgery.
examples.cn: 肝脏在手术后能再生出大部分组织。

examples.en: Fire is part of the cycle that regenerates these grasslands.
examples.cn: 火是使这些草原更新的循环的一部分。

examples.en: The trust aims to regenerate the abandoned mill district.
examples.cn: 该基金会旨在复兴废弃的磨坊区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（re）生（generate）」——再来一次生成 → 再生、更新

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」（源自 genus「出生、族类」）→ regenerare「再次产生」；英语 16 世纪进入，先用于神学，后用于生物学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: what was lost, cut or worn down is made to grow or work again, from a lizard's tail to a forest, a district, a material and a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：失去、被截断或耗损的东西重新长出或重新运转，从蜥蜴尾巴到森林、街区、材料与目标感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut stem that pushes a fresh shoot out of its wound.
core.cn: 核心意象：被截断的枝条从伤口处抽出新芽。

branches.en: LIVING REGROWTH: tissue and plants rebuild what was removed.
branches.cn: 活体再长：组织与植物重建被移除的部分。

branches.en: PLACE AND SYSTEM: districts and economies are given new activity.
branches.cn: 地点与系统：街区与经济获得新的活动。

branches.en: ECOSYSTEM: structure and function are restored, not just individuals.
branches.cn: 生态系统：恢复的是结构与功能，而非个体。

branches.en: MATERIAL: a spent medium returns to service.
branches.cn: 材料：用过的介质重新投入使用。

branches.en: SPIRIT AND RECORD: purpose is renewed, and objects are rebuilt from information.
branches.cn: 精神与记录：目标感被更新，物体依信息重建。

intro.en: The verb is Latin re- plus generare, with the usual English verb ending -ate; the noun and adjective shift to -ation and -ative.
intro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁 re- 加 generare，带常见英语动词词尾 -ate；名词与形容词分别转为 -ation 与 -ative。

latinIntro.en: Latin generare yields generate, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, generation and generous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 generare 衍生 generate、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、generation 与 generous。

items.example: The moss regenerates after the dry season.
Regeneration of the dune grass followed the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴之后沙丘草开始再生。
再生放牧模仿野生兽群。

items.meaning: a device or person that renews
items.example: The regenerator reheats the incoming air.
items.exampleCN: 回热器重新加热进入的空气。

items.meaning: a producing; one stage of descent
items.example: A generation of seedlings grew under the gap.
items.exampleCN: 林隙下长起了一代幼苗。

items.meaning: to decline from a former kind

items.example: A generous rain ended the drought.
items.exampleCN: 一场充沛的雨结束了干旱。

definition_en: a system of government or rule; a set of rules or practices in an institution; a fixed plan of diet or exercise
core_image: 广场墙上的旧标语被新海报一层层盖住
scene: 广场上的广播换了腔调，墙上的旧标语被一层层新海报盖住。The old regime fell after months of protest.
sceneCN: 这里 regime 是「政权」（第 1 个义项：一套统治制度及其政府）；句意为旧政权在数月抗议之后倒台。画面里可留意：换了腔调的广播、被盖住的旧标语。

senses.title: A system of government
senses.definition: a particular government or a system of rule, often one that is strict
senses.definitionCN: 特定的政府或统治制度，常指严厉者
senses.example: The old regime fell after months of protest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧政权在数月抗议之后倒台。
senses.why: The word is built from the Latin verb to rule, and the two letters at its front are not the prefix meaning again but the opening of that root.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由拉丁语「统治」动词构成，词首那两个字母并不是表「再次」的前缀，而是这个词根的开头。

senses.title: A set of rules
senses.definition: an ordered set of rules or practices in an institution or an activity
senses.definitionCN: 某个机构或活动中成体系的规则与做法
senses.example: The new tax regime is simpler for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 新的税收制度对小公司来说更简单。
senses.why: A government and a tax code are both systems of rule, so the same noun serves politics and administration.
senses.whyCN: 政府与税制都是「统治」的体系，因此同一个名词兼指政治与管理。

senses.title: A fixed daily plan
senses.definition: a strict plan of food, exercise, or treatment followed for health
senses.definitionCN: 为健康而严格遵循的饮食、锻炼或治疗方案
senses.example: Her doctor put her on a strict regime of rest and light exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让她严格遵守休息与轻度锻炼的规律。
senses.why: Ruling a body is like ruling a state: the same noun names a plan that keeps a person in order.
senses.whyCN: 治理身体如同治理国家：同一个名词指一套使人保持秩序的方案。

intro.en: Regime has no prefix meaning again; its first letters belong to the Latin verb regere, to rule, and the word simply names a system of rule.
intro.cn: regime 没有表「再次」的前缀；它开头的字母属于拉丁动词 regere（统治），这个词只是命名一套统治体系。

items.en: Regere meant to rule, guide, or keep straight, and it is the root of a large family of words about order.
items.cn: regere 意为统治、引导或使笔直，是一个关于秩序的大词族的根。

items.en: Regimen, built from regere, meant a rule, a guidance, or a way of managing.
items.cn: 由 regere 构成的 regimen 意为规则、引导或管理方式。

items.en: French régime named a government or a system of rule, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 régime 指政府或统治体系，英语即以这个意义借入。

items.en: The older medical use of regimen for a managed way of life passed into regime as a plan of diet and exercise.
items.cn: regimen 较早的医学用法指被管理的生活方式，这一用法传入 regime，成为饮食与锻炼的方案。

items.en: In modern politics the word often carries disapproval, naming a government that others do not accept as legitimate.
items.cn: 在现代政治中，这个词常带贬义，指他方不承认其正当性的政府。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words formed from the same ruling root; the near-meaning group gathers words for government and ordered systems.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一「统治」词根构成的词；近义组收表示政府与有序体系的词。

entries.definition: A fixed plan for health or training.
A military unit; a large group.
The body that rules a state.
The work of managing a system.

normalIntro.en: The word means a ruling order: a government, a code of rules, or a plan that rules a body.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「统治的秩序」：一个政府、一套规则，或一套管住身体的方案。

normal.en: The re in regime is not the re of again; it is the start of the root to rule.
normal.cn: regime 里的 re 不是「再次」的 re，而是「统治」词根的开头。

normal.en: A political regime is a way of ruling a country.
normal.cn: political regime 是统治一个国家的方式。

normal.en: A tax regime is a set of rules about tax.
normal.cn: tax regime 是一套关于税收的规则。

normal.en: A diet regime is a plan that rules your meals.
normal.cn: diet regime 是管住你三餐的计划。

normal.en: Do not read regime as re plus gime; the whole word comes from regere.
normal.cn: 不要把 regime 拆成 re 加 gime，整词出自 regere。

abstract.en: Every regime writes its own history, and every history hides a regime.
abstract.cn: 每个政权都写自己的历史，而每段历史都藏着一个政权。

abstract.en: A regime of rules can protect as easily as it can confine.
abstract.cn: 一套规则既能保护人，也能把人困住。

abstract.en: To keep a body in order is to govern it, and the word knows this.
abstract.cn: 让身体保持秩序就是治理它，这个词明白这一点。

examples.en: The old regime fell after months of protest.
examples.cn: 旧政权在数月抗议之后倒台。

examples.en: The new tax regime is simpler for small firms.
examples.cn: 新的税收制度对小公司来说更简单。

examples.en: Her doctor put her on a strict regime of rest and light exercise.
examples.cn: 医生让她严格遵守休息与轻度锻炼的规律。

dict_mnemonic.text: reg（统治）加 ime：统治一个国家是一套政权，统治一套事务是一种制度，统治身体是一套养生规律。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regimen（规则、管理）→ 法语 régime → 英语 regime；词首 re 属词根，不是「再次」前缀。同族有 regimen、regiment，形近的 region 也出自 regere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a ruling order; the senses move from a government, to a body of rules, to a plan that governs a life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「统治的秩序」；义项从政府，到一套规则，再到管住生活的方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: old slogans on a square wall covered layer by layer with new posters.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场墙上的旧标语被一层层新海报盖住。

branches.en: a government losing its square
a tax code in a thin booklet
a daily walk and an early bed
a rule that governs a state and a form
branches.cn: 治理国家与治理表单的同一条规则

branches.en: rules for a country and rules for a body

intro.en: A Latin verb of ruling grows a noun of guidance, and the noun enters English through French as a name for any ruling order.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「统治」的动词长出表「引导」的名词，这个名词经法语进入英语，成为一切统治秩序的名称。

latinIntro.en: The root is regere, to rule; regimen is its noun, and the first two letters of regime belong to that root, not to a prefix of repetition.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 regere（统治）；regimen 是它的名词，而 regime 的前两个字母属于这个词根，并不属于表重复的前缀。

definition_en: a large area of land with shared features; an administrative district; a part of a body or of knowledge
core_image: 火车窗外的葡萄园一块接一块向后退去
scene: 火车沿河谷向北，窗外的葡萄园一块接一块向后退去。This region is famous for its wine and its dry summers.
sceneCN: 这里 region 是「地区」（第 1 个义项：有共同特征的一片土地）；句意为这个地区以葡萄酒和干燥的夏季闻名。画面里可留意：向后退去的葡萄园、沿河谷前行的火车。

senses.title: A large area of land
senses.definition: a broad area of a country or the world that shares climate, landscape, or culture
senses.definitionCN: 一国内或世界上气候、地貌或文化相近的广阔地带
senses.example: This region is famous for its wine and its dry summers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区以葡萄酒和干燥的夏季闻名。
senses.why: The Latin noun first meant a line drawn to mark a boundary, and then the land inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最初指划出边界的一条线，后来指线内的那片土地。

senses.title: An administrative district
senses.definition: a division of a country made for government or management
senses.definitionCN: 为国家治理或管理而划分的区域
senses.example: The eastern region reports directly to the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 东部行政区直接向首都汇报。
senses.why: A boundary line drawn for rule becomes a unit of rule: the marked land turns into an office with a name.
senses.whyCN: 为统治而划出的界线变成治理的单位：被划出的土地变成了一个有名字的辖区。

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: a particular part of the body, of the mind, or of a field of knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 身体、心智或知识领域中特定的部分
senses.example: The discovery opened a new region of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现开辟了物理学的新领域。
senses.why: The idea of a bounded area is carried inward: the mind and a science are also mapped into regions.
senses.whyCN: 「有界的区域」这一观念被转向内部：心智与科学也被划分成区域。

intro.en: Region also begins with the root of ruling, not with a prefix meaning again; a regio was first a boundary drawn, then the land it enclosed.
intro.cn: region 同样以「统治」词根开头，而非表「再次」的前缀；regio 最初是一条画出的界线，随后才是界线内的土地。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or to keep straight, and a line kept straight is the first image of a region.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或使笔直，而一条画得笔直的线，正是 region 的最初意象。

items.en: Regio meant a direction, a boundary line, and then the district marked by that line.
items.cn: regio 意为方向、界线，随后指这条线划出的区域。

items.en: French région carried the geographical sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 région 把地理意义上的用法带入英语。

items.en: English used region for a broad tract of land and for a district of government.
items.cn: 英语用 region 指广阔的地带，也指行政辖区。

items.en: Later uses added parts of the body, fields of study, and the phrase in the region of for an approximate amount.
items.cn: 后来的用法又增添了身体部位、研究领域，以及表示约数的短语 in the region of。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble region in sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for a bounded area.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写与 region 相近的词；近义组收表示有界区域的词。

entries.definition: A system of faith and worship.
An administrative part of a town or country.
An area with a particular purpose or feature.

normalIntro.en: The word is a drawn line and the land inside it: first a boundary, then a place with a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条画出的线以及线内的土地：先是边界，然后是有名字的地方。

normal.en: The re in region is not the re of again; it is the start of the root to rule.
normal.cn: region 里的 re 不是「再次」的 re，而是「统治」词根的开头。

normal.en: A wine-growing region is land that shares a climate.
normal.cn: wine-growing region 是共享一种气候的土地。

normal.en: An administrative region is land drawn for government.
normal.cn: administrative region 是为治理而划出的土地。

normal.en: In the region of fifty means about fifty.
normal.cn: in the region of fifty 意为大约五十。

normal.en: Regional means belonging to such an area.
normal.cn: regional 意为属于这样一个区域的。

abstract.en: A region is made by the line we draw, not by the grass itself.
abstract.cn: 区域由我们画出的线造成，而不是由草本身造成。

abstract.en: Every science is a region with a fence that moves.
abstract.cn: 每一门科学都是一个边界会移动的区域。

abstract.en: To know a region is to know both its borders and its weather.
abstract.cn: 了解一个地区，既要了解它的边界，也要了解它的天气。

examples.en: This region is famous for its wine and its dry summers.
examples.cn: 这个地区以葡萄酒和干燥的夏季闻名。

examples.en: The eastern region reports directly to the capital.
examples.cn: 东部行政区直接向首都汇报。

examples.en: The discovery opened a new region of physics.
examples.cn: 这一发现开辟了物理学的新领域。

dict_mnemonic.text: reg（统治、划直）加 ion：被划出界线的一片土地，就是地区；再往内划，就是身体部位或知识领域。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regio（界线、区域）→ 法语 région → 英语 region；词首 re 属词根，不是「再次」前缀。同族有 regional、regionalism，形近的 regime 也出自 regere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bounded land; the senses move from a broad tract, to an administrative district, to a part of a body or a science.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「有界的土地」；义项从广阔地带，到行政辖区，再到身体或学科中的一个部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vineyards sliding past a train window, one plot after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：火车窗外一块接一块向后退去的葡萄园。

branches.en: vineyards under a dry summer
an eastern office reporting north
a new chapter in a physics book
a climate and a border on the same map
branches.cn: 同一张地图上的气候与边界

branches.en: land divided for rule and knowledge divided for study
branches.cn: 为治理而分的土地与为研究而分的知识

intro.en: A Latin verb of ruling gives a noun of direction, and a direction drawn on the ground becomes a district with a name.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「统治」的动词给出表「方向」的名词，而画在地上的一条方向线，就变成了有名字的辖区。

latinIntro.en: The root is regere, to rule; regio is its noun of direction and boundary, and the re at the front is not a prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 regere（统治）；regio 是它表方向与界线的名词，词首的 re 并不是前缀。

definition_zh: 地区的；区域性的；局部的
definition_en: relating to one particular area of a country; organized by area rather than as a whole; affecting only one part of the body
core_image: 一张大地图被彩笔划成几块，每块旁写着不同的名字
scene: 办公室墙上挂着一张大地图，被人用彩笔划成好几块。The regional government promised to build more roads in the north.
sceneCN: 这里 regional 是「地区的」（第 1 个义项：与某一地区有关的）；句意为地区政府承诺在北部多修道路。画面里可留意：被划成几块的地图、每块旁的名字。

pos.zh: 地区的；区域性的；局部的

senses.title: Relating to an area
senses.definition: connected with one particular part of a country or the world
senses.definitionCN: 与一个国家或世界的某个特定部分有关
senses.example: The regional government promised to build more roads in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 地区政府承诺在北部多修道路。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds the ending of relation to region, so it names whatever belongs to one marked stretch of land.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在 region 后面加上表关系的词尾，因此命名属于某一片被划出的土地的事物。

senses.title: Organized by area
senses.definition: arranged or divided according to area rather than as a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 按地区划分或安排，而非作为一个整体
senses.example: The company runs five regional offices instead of one head office.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司设了五个地区办事处，而不是一个总部。
senses.why: When an organization is cut along the same lines as a map, its branches are regional rather than central.
senses.whyCN: 当一个组织按照地图上的界线切分，它的分支就是区域性的，而不是中央的。

senses.title: Limited to one part
senses.definition: affecting only one part of the body, as in a regional anaesthetic
senses.definitionCN: 只影响身体的一部分，如局部麻醉
senses.example: The dentist used a regional anaesthetic so that only the jaw went numb.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医用局部麻醉，只让下颌失去知觉。
senses.why: The same idea of a bounded zone is carried into the body, where a region is an area of tissue.
senses.whyCN: 「有界区域」这一观念被带入身体，此时一个 region 就是一片组织。

intro.en: Regional is region with an adjective ending; like region, it starts from the Latin verb to rule, not from a prefix meaning again.
intro.cn: regional 是 region 加上形容词词尾；与 region 一样，它出自拉丁语「统治」动词，而非表「再次」的前缀。

items.en: Regere meant to rule or keep straight, and a straight line drawn on land is the beginning of a region.
items.cn: regere 意为统治或使笔直，而在地上画出的一条直线正是区域的起点。

items.en: Regio named a direction, then a boundary line, then the district enclosed by it.
items.cn: regio 先指方向，再指界线，最后指被这条线围出的区域。

items.en: French région carried the geographical sense of the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 région 把这个名词的地理意义带入英语。

items.en: English region named a broad tract of land and later a district of government.
items.cn: 英语 region 先指广阔地带，后指行政辖区。

items.en: The ending -al turned the noun into an adjective of belonging, so regional means of or belonging to a region.
items.cn: 词尾 -al 把名词变成表所属的形容词，于是 regional 意为属于一个地区的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble region in sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of place and locality.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写与 region 相近的词；近义组收表示地方与局部的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The word means belonging to one marked area: whatever happens inside a line on the map is regional.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「属于某片被划出的区域」：地图上一条线以内发生的事，就是 regional 的。

normal.en: Region plus al: of or belonging to a region.
normal.cn: region 加 al：属于一个地区的。

normal.en: A regional office serves one area, not the whole country.
normal.cn: regional office 服务一个地区，而不是全国。

normal.en: Regional dialect is speech that stays inside its borders.
normal.cn: regional dialect 是留在自己边界内的说话方式。

normal.en: Regional anaesthetic numbs one part of the body only.
normal.cn: regional anaesthetic 只麻醉身体的一个部位。

normal.en: The re at the front belongs to the root to rule, not to a prefix of repetition.
normal.cn: 词首的 re 属于「统治」词根，不是表重复的前缀。

abstract.en: A regional identity is a border that people choose to keep.
abstract.cn: 地区认同是人们选择保留的一道边界。

abstract.en: What is regional can be rich precisely because it is not universal.
abstract.cn: 地方性的东西之所以丰厚，正因为它并不普遍。

abstract.en: Every map is a set of decisions about where one region ends.
abstract.cn: 每一张地图都是关于「区域在哪里结束」的一连串决定。

examples.en: The regional government promised to build more roads in the north.
examples.cn: 地区政府承诺在北部多修道路。

examples.en: The company runs five regional offices instead of one head office.
examples.cn: 这家公司设了五个地区办事处，而不是一个总部。

examples.en: The dentist used a regional anaesthetic so that only the jaw went numb.
examples.cn: 牙医用局部麻醉，只让下颌失去知觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: region（地区）加 al（形容词尾）：与某个地区有关的、按地区划分的、只限一个部位的，都叫 regional。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regio（界线、区域）→ 法语 région → 英语 region ＋ -al → regional；词首 re 属词根，不是「再次」前缀。同族有 region、regionalism、regionally。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging to a bounded area; the senses move from a district of a country, to a way of organizing by districts, to one part of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于有界的区域」；义项从国内的一个地区，到按地区组织，再到身体的一个部位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall map cut into coloured blocks, each with a name beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张大地图被彩笔划成几块，每块旁写着不同的名字。

intro.en: The noun of a marked area takes an adjective ending, and the result describes anything that belongs inside one boundary.
intro.cn: 表「被划出的区域」的名词接上形容词词尾，结果便描述一切属于某条边界之内的事物。

latinIntro.en: The root is regere, to rule; regio is the noun, and -al makes the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 regere（统治）；regio 是名词，-al 构成形容词。
